main_text.p: da Rep.utque confules feu quis alius regimen fuscriperet, vero quoque & honesto fidem dempsit. Plura de excessu Tiberianæ simulationis pete ex Arcanis regnorum: pag. 183.
main_text.head: XII. Fœcunda adulationum vanitas.
main_text.p: Priores enim superare honorum cumulatione sequentes conantur, ut fermè amat posterior adulatio. Quo titulorum congestæ vanitates in Germania excreverint, ut jam & magnitudine & multitudine sua laborent, viri sapientioris animi vident, ridént, aut ingemiscunt.
main_text.head: XIII. Corrupta in miraculum historia prudenti examine arguitur.
main_text.p: Multos non vera, sed fabulosa in legenda historia juvant. Hinc Vera Luciani, nihil minus quam vera, Historia; hinc qui inscribitur liber Die wahrhaftige Lügen/hinc qui Gallis dicuntur Les Romans & Amadis deVanitatum delicia. Gaule tenacius lectorem, quam res nudè descriptæ attinent. Ex hac prodigiosæ novitatis aviditate in historiam Romanam irrepsit fabulosa de ortu Romuli & Remi narratio: nec plus fidei apud me repertura, toties bos in Campanis locuta. Similibus historiæ portentis Tacitus accensèt, quæ de Drusi interitu spargebantur, monitum Tiberium, vitaret potionem, quæ prima ei apud filium epulanti offerretur, ea fraude tum senem, postquam convivium inierat, exceptum poculum Druso tradidisse. atq; illo ignaro & juveniliter hauriente, auctam suspicionem, tanquam metu & pudore sibimet irrogaret mortem, quam patri struxerat. Quod ubi recensuit, hoc argumento Cornelius refutat.

p.i: Quis enim mediocri prudentia, nedum Tiberius, tantis rebus exercitus, inaudito filio exitium offerret, idque sua manu, & nullo adpœnitendum regressu? Quin potius ministrum veneni excruciaret, auctorem exquireret, infita denique etiam in extraneos contatione[?] &

page.notes: The printed text is partly damaged at the right edge of the lines and in the last line of the page, where the word after "contatione" is cut off by the scan. Two words in the body text are read with some doubt: "contatione" (the reading "contagione" is also possible) and "Druso" (the second "o" looks like a different letter). The word "ridént" is read from a faint print. The margin note "Vanitatum delicia." was placed beside the line "Amadis de"; the printed line "delicia." belongs to the same note. The top line under the running head is a note carried over from the previous page, set in italic. The head "XII" and "XIII" are given as chapter numbers with their titles.
